question: what are the existing approaches?

evidence: We will refer to our model as EGEL (Embedding GEographic Locations), and will consider the following variants. EGEL-Tags only uses the information from the Flickr tags (i.e. component INLINEFORM0 ), without using any negative examples and without feature selection. EGEL-Tags+NS is similar to EGEL-Tags but with the addition of negative examples. EGEL-KL(Tags+NS) additionally considers term selection. EGEL-All is our full method, i.e. it additionally uses the structured information. We also consider the following baselines. BOW-Tags represents locations using a bag-of-words representation, using the same tag weighting as the embedding model. BOW-KL(Tags) uses the same representation but after term selection, using the same KL-based method as the embedding model. BOW-All combines the bag-of-words representation with the structured information, encoded as proposed in BIBREF7 . GloVe uses the objective from the original GloVe model for learning location vectors, i.e. this variant differs from EGEL-Tags in that instead of INLINEFORM1 we use the number of co-occurrences of tag INLINEFORM2 near location INLINEFORM3 , measured as INLINEFORM4 .

title: Embedding Geographic Locations for Modelling the Natural Environment using Flickr Tags and Structured Data
answer_short: Existing approaches include using bag-of-words representations, word embedding models (e.g., Skip-gram, CBOW, GloVe), spatially smoothed pointwise mutual information, and methods combining geographic coordinates with textual or categorical features.
answer_rationale: The retrieved documents describe various existing approaches for representing geographic locations, including bag-of-words models (e.g., BOW-Tags), word embedding models (e.g., Skip-gram, CBOW, GloVe), spatial smoothing techniques, and methods that integrate textual or categorical features with geographic data. These are explicitly mentioned in Text 1, Text 2, Text 6, and Text 7.
